## EMST role: Wildland fire operations (crew to supervisor) (state variant, lead level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.35, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R06-wildland-fire-operations/state:523A`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Suppress wildland fire safely with ground tactics and resources — lead L4 *(distinguishing)*
- Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments — lead L4
- Operate chainsaws and other power equipment safely in field conditions — lead L3
- Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids — lead L3
- Lead field crews and transfer field judgment to novices — lead L4
- Predict fire behaviour from fuels, weather and topography for operations and planning — lead L3
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — lead L4
- Provide first aid and emergency medical care in remote field settings — lead L3
- Communicate during field emergencies and report incidents — lead L3
- Use and maintain hand tools safely for field work — lead L2
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — lead L1
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — lead L1
- Assess tree risk and structural condition — lead L2
- Evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards — lead L3
- Conduct prescribed fire from burn planning through ignition, holding and evaluation — lead L3
- Drive and operate field vehicles safely on unpaved roads and off road — lead L2

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Execute a firing operation that removes fuel between the control line and the fire under the firing boss's direction — 8.3% *(critical)*
- Size up a new fire's fuels, weather, topography and values at risk to recommend initial attack tactics — 8.3% *(critical)*
- Direct a crew's tactical assignment, adjusting tactics when observed fire behaviour or weather departs from the briefing — 8.3% *(critical)*
- Lead a small crew through a field day, matching tasks to skill and checking novice work early and often — 8.3%
- Brief incident personnel on expected fire behaviour and weather trends, highlighting watch-out situations for each division — 4.2%
- Compare modelled fire behaviour with observed behaviour during an incident, adjusting predictions and recording each discrepancy — 4.2%
- Inspect a chainsaw before use for chain brake, chain catcher, throttle lock and chain condition, removing a defective saw from service — 4.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Brief a field crew on the day's site hazards, escape routes, safety zones and communication plan before work begins — 4.2% *(critical)*
- Drive a four-wheel-drive vehicle on unpaved and off-road routes, selecting gear, speed and line for mud, sand, snow, rock and water crossings — 4.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Assess hazard trees around a field work site or crew area before work starts, flagging trees that need removal or an exclusion zone — 4.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Decide whether a novice is ready for independent field work from observed performance against stated criteria, recording the sign-off — 4.2%
- Run an after-action review with the crew at the end of a field operation, recording what happened, why and what will change — 4.2%

*Credential gates (draft):* Wildland fire position qualifications under the interagency standard (e.g., firefighter, burn boss, incident commander types) (required)

## EMST role: Natural resource and environmental programme manager (state variant, lead level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.4, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R13-resource-program-manager/state:523A`). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Formulate, justify and execute public budgets across appropriations cycles — lead L4 *(distinguishing)*
- Brief decision-makers and elected officials for authoritative decisions — lead L4
- Govern enterprise environmental data and AI portfolios — lead L4
- Elicit, document and transfer tacit and institutional knowledge before people leave — lead L3
- Deliver environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality — lead L3
- Design and administer cross-jurisdictional stewardship agreements — lead L4
- Assess the durability and reversal risk of policy choices and time actions to policy windows — lead L4
- Administer contracts, grants and intergovernmental agreements — lead L4
- Prepare and revise management plans for publicly held lands — lead L4
- Design developmental work experiences that preserve the formation of professional judgment — lead L4
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — lead L3
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — lead L3
- Design human-in-the-loop review for AI-assisted environmental workflows — lead L3
- Specify, evaluate and accept AI and analytics services in procurement — lead L3
- Evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards — lead L4
- Develop proposals and grant applications for environmental work — lead L3
- Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance — lead L3
- Apply systems thinking across ecological, institutional and technical systems — lead L3
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — lead L4
- Navigate legislative and governing-body processes for environmental programs — lead L4

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Prepare a program budget request and justification linking each funding increment to outputs and outcomes the budget office can verify — 10.2% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Reconcile program obligations and expenditures against appropriations, agreements and fee accounts each month, flagging any use outside purpose or period — 6.7% *(needed at entry)*
- Write a decision memo for an accountable official, stating the decision required, options, evidence, risks and a recommendation within two pages — 6.7% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Coordinate an interdisciplinary team drafting a forest, range or refuge management plan, assigning plan components and reconciling conflicting resource objectives — 6.7% *(critical)*
- Prepare a continuing-resolution and funding-lapse contingency plan, ranking program activities by legal requirement and consequence of delay — 3.4% *(critical)*
- Brief appropriations staff or a governing board on a program budget request, answering questions with figures traceable to the justification — 3.4%
- Assess the reversal risk of a program's key instruments, recording the evidence, the likely triggers and a contingency for each high-risk instrument — 3.4%
- Brief a decision-maker orally on a pending decision under time pressure, answering questions and stating where the evidence is uncertain — 3.4% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Prepare a staff report for a governing body's public meeting, stating findings, options and the legal basis for each recommended action — 3.4%
- Track bills, ordinances and appropriations measures affecting the program, summarizing each relevant provision's effect on program operations — 3.4% *(needed at entry)*
- Write a dated change notice explaining what a new rule, guidance or court decision changes for staff, its effective dates and the work in progress it affects — 3.4% *(needed at entry)*
- Draft a memorandum of understanding or interagency agreement that assigns shared responsibilities, resources and decision rights for a joint program — 3.4%
